sentences.text:
% 21.02.2023 CRL.M.A. 4662/2023 (exemption)
1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973(Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the petitioners seeking quashing of FIR bearing no. 376/2012 registered at Police Station Anand Vihar, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 509/506/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
4. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. Deepak Vohra and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Arun Ahlawat from Police Station Anand Vihar, Delhi.
5. Brief facts of the present case are that petitioners were employed at clerical position at Ideal Institute of Management and Technology.

entities.text: Ideal Institute of Management and Technology
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Respondent no. 2 was a student at Ideal Institute of Management and Technology.

entities.text: Ideal Institute of Management and Technology
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The complainant/respondent no. 2 applied for Character Certificate with the said Institute on 21.09.2012.
Her father had given the requisite application to the institute in the morning at about 10.30 AM.

It has been alleged that despite being suffering from fever, the complainant and her father reached the institute at about 4.30 PM and the petitioner Amit refused to deliver the character certificate.

On being questioned, petitioner Amit allegedly got angry, started abusing and criminally intimidating the father of the complainant till both of them (Complainant Amit Mittal And Anr vs State And Ors on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7175311/
1 and father) got out of the college.

entities.text: Complainant Amit Mittal And Anr vs State And Ors on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereafter, upon the complaint of respondent no. 2, an FIR bearing no. 376/2012 was registered at Police Station Anand Vihar, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 509/506/34 of IPC against the petitioners.

6. On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.
It is also stated by respondent no. 2 and 3 that the entire dispute has been settled amicably after the petitioners have tendered apology.

In terms of the settlement,
respondent nos. 2 and 3 does not wish to pursue the abovenoted FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto and petitioners also affirms before this Court that such misbehaviour will not take place in future and have also shown remorse.

7. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings,
rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

8. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 376/2012 registered at Police Station Anand Vihar, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 509/506/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
9. In view of above, the present petition stands disposed of.
10. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J FEBRUARY 21, 2023/ns
